papers.abstract_zh: 目的：肠外致病性大肠杆菌（Extraintestinal pathogenic Escherichia coli, ExPEC）是血流感染和尿路感染的主要病原体，常表现为多重耐药，且与超广谱β-内酰胺酶（extended-spectrum beta-lactamases, ESBLs）的产生相关。本研究旨在揭示日本北部地区ExPEC的克隆结构、多样性及其与抗菌药物耐药性（antimicrobial resistance, AMR）特征、决定因子和遗传特性的关系。方法：基于MLST方案，对ExPEC临床分离株进行系统发育群和序列类型（sequence type, ST）鉴定。采用PCR和测序技术鉴定AMR决定因子、毒力因子和CRISPR-Cas系统，并通过肉汤微量稀释法进行抗菌药物敏感性试验。结果：在6个月内共收集454株ExPEC分离株（150株来自血液，304株来自尿液/其他标本）。主要系统发育群为B2（79.5%），其余为D（9.9%）、B1（5.7%）、F（3.1%）及其他群（A、C、G；合计1.8%）。在鉴定的68个ST中，ST131最常见（33.7%），其次为ST95（15.6%）、ST357（9.9%）、ST1193（7%）和ST73（4%），均属于系统发育群B2。在17%的分离株中检测到5种ESBL基因，包括优势基因bla(CTX-M-15)或bla(CTX-M-27)，这些分离株主要属于ST131复合体。CRISPR-Cas I-E型主要存在于系统发育群B1和D中，而I-F型存在于系统发育群B2的3个ST中。结论：ST357、ST1193及动物相关克隆的潜在流行增加，揭示了日本北部地区ExPEC的新克隆特征。

papers.title: Application of emerging technologies in the antiviral field.
papers.authors: Zhang, Xiaoyan; Zhang, Lele; Guo, Tengda; Du, Wenjuan; Wang, Shen; Li, Yongtao
papers.one_liner_zh: 综述AI、基因编辑、类器官和合成生物学在抗病毒领域的应用，虽涉及AI分子设计但未聚焦无序蛋白/IDR或PPI机制建模，与本课题关联较弱。
papers.abstract: Viral diseases pose a serious threat to global public health, agriculture, and biosecurity. Conventional antiviral strategies are often limited by an incomplete understanding of disease mechanisms, poor targeting precision, and slow response times. Emerging technologies are now reshaping the landscape of antiviral research. This review examines the roles of four key frontiers, including organoid models, gene editing, AI-driven molecular design, and synthetic biology. Organoids provide physiologically relevant platforms that model virus-host interactions and disease progression. Viral infections remain a major challenge to human and animal health, agriculture, and biosecurity. Progress in antiviral research is constrained by the complexity of viral pathogenesis, the diversity and rapid evolution of viruses, and the limited translational relevance of some traditional model systems. Recent advances in organoid technology, gene editing, artificial intelligence, and synthetic biology are expanding the toolkit available for antiviral research and development. In this review, we discuss how these four technological frontiers contribute to disease modeling, target discovery, molecular design, and translational innovation. Organoids, in particular, provide physiologically relevant systems for investigating viral infection, tissue tropism, host responses, and pathogenesis. Gene editing tools, such as CRISPR, enable precise manipulation of host and viral genomes, facilitating the development of resistant organisms and next-generation vaccine platforms. AI technologies, including AlphaFold for structure prediction and platforms for de novo protein design, address long-standing bottlenecks in structural biology and offer powerful means to engineer antiviral proteins, antibodies, and vaccine antigens. Synthetic biology, guided by the Design-Build-Test-Learn cycle, integrates computational design, genetic assembly, and functional validation into a cohesive pipeline. Together, these technologies form a synergistic workflow that spans disease modeling, target discovery, molecular design, construction, testing, and iterative optimization. This integrated approach is shifting antiviral development from traditional empirical methods toward more precise, intelligent strategies. The review also highlights ongoing challenges in integration and scalability, stressing that high-quality biological datasets and stronger interdisciplinary collaboration are essential for realizing translational potential. By presenting a cohesive view of these converging methodologies, this review offers a framework to guide the intelligent evolution of antiviral strategies in both human and animal health.
papers.abstract_zh: 病毒性疾病对全球公共卫生、农业和生物安全构成严重威胁。传统抗病毒策略常因对疾病机制理解不完整、靶向精度不足以及响应速度缓慢而受到限制。新兴技术正在重塑抗病毒研究的格局。本综述探讨了四个关键前沿领域的作用，包括类器官模型 (organoid models)、基因编辑 (gene editing)、人工智能驱动的分子设计 (AI-driven molecular design) 和合成生物学 (synthetic biology)。类器官提供了模拟病毒-宿主相互作用和疾病进展的生理相关平台。病毒感染仍然是对人类和动物健康、农业及生物安全的重大挑战。抗病毒研究的进展受到病毒致病机制的复杂性、病毒的多样性和快速进化，以及某些传统模型系统转化相关性有限的制约。类器官技术、基因编辑、人工智能和合成生物学的最新进展正在扩展可用于抗病毒研究和开发的工具库。在本综述中，我们讨论了这四个技术前沿如何促进疾病建模、靶点发现、分子设计和转化创新。特别是，类器官为研究病毒感染、组织嗜性、宿主反应和致病机制提供了生理相关系统。基因编辑工具，如CRISPR，能够精确操作宿主和病毒基因组，促进抗性生物体和下一代疫苗平台的开发。人工智能技术，包括用于结构预测的AlphaFold和用于从头蛋白质设计的平台，解决了结构生物学中长期存在的瓶颈，并为设计抗病毒蛋白、抗体和疫苗抗原提供了强大手段。合成生物学在“设计-构建-测试-学习”循环 (Design-Build-Test-Learn cycle) 的指导下，将计算设计、基因组装和功能验证整合成一个连贯的流程。这些技术共同形成了一个协同工作流，涵盖疾病建模、靶点发现、分子设计、构建、测试和迭代优化。这种整合方法正在将抗病毒开发从传统的经验方法转向更精确、更智能的策略。本综述还强调了整合和可扩展性方面的持续挑战，指出高质量生物数据集和更强的跨学科合作对于实现转化潜力至关重要。通过呈现这些汇聚方法的连贯视角，本综述提供了一个框架，以指导人类和动物健康领域抗病毒策略的智能化演进。

papers.title: Regulatory Evolution and the Genetic Basis of Human Brain Expansion.
papers.authors: Hettiarachchi, Nilmini
papers.one_liner_zh: 该综述探讨人类大脑扩张的调控进化与基因调控元件，不涉及无序蛋白、蛋白互作或AI/物理模拟方法，与本课题无关。
papers.abstract: The evolution of the human brain is characterized by profound changes in structure and function, despite relatively limited divergence in protein-coding genes compared to other primates. This paradox has led to increasing recognition of gene regulatory elements (GREs) as primary drivers of evolutionary innovation. In this review, we synthesize current knowledge on the role of conserved noncoding elements (CNEs), human accelerated regions (HARs), and transposable element (TE)-derived sequences in shaping gene regulatory networks (GRNs) underlying brain development. Comparative analyses across humans and closely related primates, including the chimpanzee, gorilla, and orangutan, reveal that while core regulatory architectures are highly conserved, subtle changes in regulatory elements drive species-specific gene expression patterns. We highlight how CNEs provide a stable regulatory framework, whereas HARs and TE-derived elements introduce lineage-specific modifications that fine-tune neurodevelopmental processes. Advances in functional genomics, including CRISPR-based perturbations, massively parallel reporter assays, and single-cell multi-omics, have enabled direct interrogation of regulatory function, linking sequence variation to cellular phenotypes. Furthermore, we discuss how regulatory evolution contributes to both cognitive innovation and susceptibility to neurological disorders. Despite significant progress, challenges remain in establishing causal relationships between regulatory variation and phenotypic outcomes. Future integration of multi-omics data and comparative models will be essential for resolving these complexities. Together, this review provides a comprehensive framework for understanding the molecular basis of primate brain evolution through the lens of gene regulation.
papers.abstract_zh: 人类大脑的进化以结构和功能的深刻变化为特征，尽管与其他灵长类动物相比，其蛋白质编码基因的差异相对有限。这一悖论使得基因调控元件（gene regulatory elements, GREs）逐渐被认识到是进化创新的主要驱动力。在本综述中，我们综合了关于保守非编码元件（conserved noncoding elements, CNEs）、人类加速区域（human accelerated regions, HARs）以及转座元件（transposable element, TE）衍生序列在塑造大脑发育的基因调控网络（gene regulatory networks, GRNs）中作用的现有知识。跨人类及近缘灵长类动物（包括黑猩猩、大猩猩和猩猩）的比较分析揭示，尽管核心调控架构高度保守，但调控元件的细微变化驱动了物种特异的基因表达模式。我们强调CNEs如何提供稳定的调控框架，而HARs和TE衍生元件则引入谱系特异的修饰，精细调控神经发育过程。功能基因组学的进展，包括基于CRISPR的扰动、大规模平行报告基因检测和单细胞多组学，已能够直接探究调控功能，将序列变异与细胞表型联系起来。此外，我们讨论了调控进化如何同时促进认知创新和对神经系统疾病的易感性。尽管取得了显著进展，但在建立调控变异与表型结果之间的因果关系方面仍存在挑战。未来多组学数据与比较模型的整合对于解决这些复杂性至关重要。总之，本综述通过基因调控的视角，为理解灵长类动物大脑进化的分子基础提供了一个全面的框架。

papers.title: Aire deficiency disrupts thymic architecture but preserves TCRVbeta repertoire diversity while altering thymic output.
papers.authors: Matos, Adriana Arruda; Araujo, Itaua Leston; Munuera, Matheus Dominato; Palma, Patricia Viana Bonini; Bonaldo, Camila; Brito, Leticia Agrelli; Mendes-da-Cruz, Daniella Areas; Savino, Wilson; Passos, Geraldo Aleixo; Donadi, Eduardo Antonio
papers.one_liner_zh: 该研究探讨Aire缺陷对胸腺结构和T细胞输出的影响，不涉及无序蛋白、蛋白互作或AI/物理模拟方法，与本课题无关。
papers.abstract: The autoimmune regulator (Aire) gene is essential for the establishment of central tolerance by promoting the ectopic expression of tissue-restricted antigens in medullary thymic epithelial cells (mTECs). Although Aire deficiency impairs negative selection, its impact on thymic architecture, output, and early T cell development remains incompletely understood. Here, we used a murine Aire-deficient model carrying a CRISPR-Cas9-induced deletion within exon 6, disrupting the SAND domain, to investigate the consequences of Aire loss on thymic structure and function. Aire-deficient mice exhibited focal alopecia and marked disorganization of the thymic medulla. T cell receptor excision circle (TREC) analyses revealed altered peripheral TREC dynamics and a reduced sj/betaTREC ratio, indicating altered thymic output and impaired intrathymic precursor expansion. Complementary flow-cytometric analysis showed a significant reduction in the proportion of CD4(+)CD8(+) double-positive thymocytes in heterozygous mutants, supporting altered intrathymic maturation. Serum IL-27, IL-28B, and IL-31 were decreased in homozygous mutants, whereas IL-22 and IL-23 remained unchanged. Despite these alterations, TCRVbeta repertoire sequencing revealed no significant differences in rearrangements, clonality, or V/J gene usage. Together, these findings indicate that Aire deficiency disrupts thymic architecture and output, while preserving overall TCR repertoire diversity.
papers.abstract_zh: 自身免疫调节因子（Aire）基因通过促进髓质胸腺上皮细胞（mTECs）中组织限制性抗原的异位表达，对建立中枢耐受至关重要。尽管Aire缺陷会损害阴性选择，但其对胸腺结构、输出及早期T细胞发育的影响仍不完全清楚。在此，我们使用携带CRISPR-Cas9诱导的外显子6缺失（破坏SAND结构域）的鼠Aire缺陷模型，研究Aire缺失对胸腺结构和功能的影响。Aire缺陷小鼠表现出局灶性脱发和胸腺髓质的显著紊乱。T细胞受体切除环（TREC）分析显示外周TREC动力学改变以及sj/betaTREC比值降低，表明胸腺输出改变和胸腺内前体细胞扩增受损。补充的流式细胞术分析显示，杂合突变体中CD4(+)CD8(+)双阳性胸腺细胞的比例显著降低，支持胸腺内成熟过程的改变。纯合突变体血清中IL-27、IL-28B和IL-31水平降低，而IL-22和IL-23保持不变。尽管存在这些改变，TCRVbeta库测序显示重排、克隆性或V/J基因使用无显著差异。综合这些发现表明，Aire缺陷破坏了胸腺结构和输出，同时保留了整体TCR库多样性。

papers.title: Functional Annotation of the Major Histocompatibility Complex Locus.
papers.authors: Bounds, Lexi R; Barrera, Alejandro; Ter Weele, Maria; Liu, Siyan; Wu, Euphy; Li, Shengyu; Venukuttan, Revathy; Rai, Ruhi; Mu, Wancen; Iglesias, Nahid; Giusti-Rodriguez, Paola; Reddy, Timothy E; Li, Yun; Gordan, Raluca; Allen, Andrew S; Love, Michael I; Sullivan, Patrick F; Crawford, Gregory E; Gersbach, Charles A
papers.journal: bioRxiv : the preprint server for biology
papers.one_liner_zh: 该文通过CRISPR筛选和单细胞转录组研究MHC基因座的调控元件-基因连接，不涉及无序蛋白、蛋白互作或AI/物理模拟方法，与本课题无关。
papers.abstract: The human major histocompatibility complex (MHC) locus has the greatest density of disease-associations in the human genome, including links to over 100 polygenic disorders. Its complex haplotype structure, rich gene density, and high degree of linkage disequilibrium combine to make deciphering the gene regulatory logic of the MHC locus extremely challenging. Employing complementary high-throughput CRISPR interference (CRISPRi) and activation (CRISPRa) epigenetic screens coupled with single-cell transcriptome profiling across three distinct human cell types, we identified hundreds of new connections between cis -regulatory elements (CREs) and their target genes in this locus. These CRE-gene links are largely cell type-specific and act as enhancers. Additionally, some CREs have complex features, including harboring both active and repressive histone marks, lacking chromatin accessibility, targeting multiple genes, or acting as silencers. Computational methods fail to predict a majority of these CRE-gene connections. These findings emphasize the potential for functional perturbation experiments to dissect complex loci and reveal shared and cell type-specific regulatory mechanisms relevant to genomics of complex diseases. Collectively, this study provides a unique resource for understanding the complex regulatory landscape within the MHC locus and supports the need for creating new models that encompass CRE-gene interactions, cell type-specific gene expression, and disease genetics in the noncoding genome.
papers.abstract_zh: 人类主要组织相容性复合体（major histocompatibility complex, MHC）基因座在人类基因组中具有最高的疾病关联密度，包括与超过100种多基因疾病的关联。其复杂的单倍型结构、丰富的基因密度以及高度的连锁不平衡（linkage disequilibrium）共同使得解析MHC基因座的基因调控逻辑极具挑战性。通过结合互补的高通量CRISPR干扰（CRISPRi）和激活（CRISPRa）表观遗传学筛选，并在三种不同的人类细胞类型中进行单细胞转录组分析，我们鉴定出该基因座中数百个新的顺式调控元件（cis-regulatory elements, CREs）与其靶基因之间的连接。这些CRE-基因连接主要具有细胞类型特异性，并发挥增强子（enhancer）功能。此外，部分CREs具有复杂特征，包括同时携带激活性和抑制性组蛋白修饰、缺乏染色质可及性、靶向多个基因，或发挥沉默子（silencer）作用。计算方法无法预测这些CRE-基因连接中的大多数。这些发现强调了功能扰动实验在解析复杂基因座中的潜力，并揭示了与复杂疾病基因组学相关的共享及细胞类型特异性调控机制。总体而言，本研究为理解MHC基因座内的复杂调控景观提供了独特资源，并支持了在非编码基因组中建立涵盖CRE-基因相互作用、细胞类型特异性基因表达及疾病遗传学的新模型的必要性。

papers.title: Artificial Intelligence in Biomaterials: Revolutionizing Design and Manufacturing.
papers.authors: Liu, Yichen; Wang, Zhiting; Wei, Haojie; Ding, Xili; Fan, Yubo
papers.journal: Journal of biomedical materials research. Part A
papers.one_liner_zh: 该综述讨论AI在生物材料设计制造中的应用，但对象为生物材料而非无序蛋白/IDR，未涉及PPI或互作机制建模，与本课题无关。
papers.abstract: Biomaterials are indispensable to modern healthcare, yet their development remains hindered by traditional trial-and-error approaches that are costly, time-intensive, and inefficient. Artificial intelligence (AI) offers a powerful alternative, but most existing reviews treat AI merely as a computational tool for property prediction rather than as a systemic driver of innovation across the entire biomaterials' lifecycle. This review bridges that gap by providing a holistic, end-to-end perspective that integrates AI-driven design, intelligent manufacturing, and clinical translation into a unified framework. We systematically examine how AI-powered predictive modeling and structure-function optimization are reshaping the discovery of polymers, proteins, drug carriers, and tissue scaffolds, while also driving breakthroughs in 3D bioprinting, laser processing, composite manufacturing, and genetically programmed bio-fabrication. Recognizing that computational promise does not automatically translate into clinical reality, we critically evaluate persistent barriers such as data scarcity, poor data quality, the interpretability-accuracy trade-off, and regulatory uncertainties, and discuss strategies to overcome them through Explainable AI and rigorous validation protocols. Looking forward, we explore the convergence of AI with quantum computing and CRISPR (Clustered Regularly Interspaced Short Palindromic Repeats) gene editing, which together could enable a new generation of multifunctional, responsive biomaterials. By synthesizing advances across the full lifecycle and offering a structured framework for selecting AI methodologies tailored to specific biomaterials challenges, this review aims to serve as both a comprehensive resource and a strategic roadmap for translating computational innovation into tangible clinical impact.
papers.abstract_zh: 生物材料是现代医疗保健不可或缺的组成部分，但其发展仍受限于传统的试错法——这些方法成本高昂、耗时且效率低下。人工智能（AI）提供了一种强大的替代方案，但现有的大多数综述仅将AI视为用于性质预测的计算工具，而非贯穿整个生物材料生命周期的系统性创新驱动力。本综述通过提供一种整体性、端到端的视角，将AI驱动的设计、智能制造和临床转化整合到一个统一框架中，从而弥补了这一空白。我们系统性地审视了AI驱动的预测建模和结构-功能优化如何重塑聚合物、蛋白质、药物载体和组织支架的发现过程，同时推动3D生物打印、激光加工、复合材料制造和基因编程生物制造领域的突破。认识到计算潜力并不会自动转化为临床现实，我们批判性地评估了数据稀缺、数据质量差、可解释性-准确性权衡以及监管不确定性等持续存在的障碍，并讨论了通过可解释AI（Explainable AI）和严格验证协议来克服这些障碍的策略。展望未来，我们探讨了AI与量子计算及CRISPR（Clustered Regularly Interspaced Short Palindromic Repeats）基因编辑的融合，这些技术共同有望催生新一代多功能、响应性生物材料。通过综合全生命周期的进展，并提供针对特定生物材料挑战选择AI方法的结构化框架，本综述旨在成为将计算创新转化为切实临床影响的综合资源与战略路线图。
